metadata.coverage: Audited union of identified direct questions, selected policy-relevant elections/recalls, state-control changes and selected bills. Not a certified exhaustive national election census.
counting_rules: Every record retains its scope, source quality and date. This is an audited research inventory, not a certified exhaustive registry of all local elections nationwide.
Count questions, elections and elected offices separately. Multiple questions in one town do not represent distinct groups of voters.
Use yes/(yes+no) for ordinary question shares; keep blank/overvote counts and charter thresholds separately. Do not infer turnout from valid votes alone.
Candidate victories cannot isolate a data-center issue's causal effect. Advisory votes are public opinions with no automatic legal ban.
Current officeholders and incoming elected officials are different time states; November wins do not retroactively enact proposals.

base_census.coverage: Audited union of named national trackers plus separately tagged additional direct/adjacent votes; not a verified exhaustive national inventory of every local election.
base_census.unique_voters: Not computable from summed question totals; jurisdictions and ballot questions overlap.
base_census.method: One row per question. Preserve yes/no polarity, advisory status, event dates, source update dates, missing data and conflicts. Most Nov3 returns remain unofficial at cutoff. Primary_counts_verified means counts read in primary text or visually checked against a downloaded official return, not certification. Restriction_outcome describes the direction of the successful ballot choice; for advisory votes this does not mean a legal restriction was enacted.

gaps.next_step: Replace snapshots after county/state canvasses; preserve prior versions.

gaps.impact: A party label or a general-election victory does not quantify voter support for every AI/data-center policy.
gaps.next_step: Maintain campaign positions as sourced attributes, separate from candidate vote counts.

gaps.next_step: Use clerk canvass exports and current bill text before publication.

gaps.next_step: Show the denominator in every tooltip; never label summed ballot questions unique voters.

gaps.next_step: Default dashboard filters to targeted data-center questions, with explicit toggles.

gaps.impact: Filed proposals and campaign promises are not laws. Many 2025–26 bills need reintroduction.
gaps.next_step: Refresh filing histories and operative dates after session opening.

gaps.impact: Uncalled seats and disputed aggregate reports remain. Minnesota started tied; Virginia changed governor in 2025.
gaps.next_step: Refresh official chamber totals without rewriting historical classifications.

gaps.impact: Surveys use different questions, populations and weights. State overall sample sizes are not question bases.
gaps.next_step: Keep survey IDs and field dates visible; suppress misleading time-series comparisons.

gaps.impact: Approval may affect only future or unvested projects; litigation and permit rights can limit practical effect.
gaps.next_step: Track legal effect separately from election outcome, especially Emporia, Piqua and Trenton.
